column4: and notice below is fictional and synthetic. Nothing here describes a real event

column16: Synthetic example: suggested a higher antihypertensive dose for an older patient with heart failure without checking kidney function; a clinician caught it before ordering.

column12: Fictional audit of diabetes advice quality (synthetic)
column16: Synthetic example: an audit rated type 2 diabetes advice lower for one ethnicity group than for others. No harm was reported.
Synthetic example: answers on mental health conditions became less specific after a model update; the developer restored the earlier configuration.
Synthetic example: an adult antibiotic dose was suggested for a child with pneumonia. Corrected by the care team; the rule set was fixed and the case closed.
Synthetic example: a draft discharge letter after a heart attack listed a follow-up test that was never ordered.
Synthetic example: some draft letters for chronic lung disease named an inhaler the patient did not use; a prompt change reduced it and reviewers check medication lists.
Synthetic example: a draft letter for chronic kidney disease stated a kidney function value that was not in the record.
Synthetic example: depression and anxiety suggestions were less complete for women in a fairness evaluation. No harm was reported.
Synthetic example: sepsis risk estimates for older patients drifted lower over three months, which could delay escalation.
Synthetic example: a small lung nodule was labelled benign and follow-up was delayed. Double reading of flagged scans now applies.
Synthetic example: melanoma was missed more often on darker skin in a validation study, which could delay diagnosis.
Synthetic example: the developer recalled one app version after finding that photos taken in low light were scored as low risk.
Synthetic example: agreement with dermatologists on actinic keratosis fell slightly after a camera change. Under review.
Synthetic example: draft letters for heart conditions sometimes repeated an old echocardiogram result as new. Fixed and closed.
Synthetic example: older patients with atypical chest pain or stroke signs were given a lower triage category than the protocol asks for.
Synthetic example: the triage form could not record the weight of young children, so staff entered it in free text.
